Solar Pulse | Software, AI & Space Technologies

Solar Pulse is a technology team passionate about software development, artificial intelligence, and space exploration. We aim to create innovative solutions by combining science and technology.

As part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we focus on astronaut health, AI-powered systems, and data analysis.

We welcome creative, motivated individuals interested in programming, AI, UI/UX design, and scientific research.

Our mission is to learn, innovate, and shape the future of technology together!

Our project aims to monitor health indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), sleep patterns, and physical activity, while helping astronauts plan their daily tasks and receive personalized assistance through the **Qwen AI model**.

details:
Solar Pulse — Project Details

Project Purpose and the Problem We Aim to Solve

Solar Pulse is an AI-powered health monitoring and mission management platform developed to support astronauts' physical and mental well-being during long-duration space missions, organize their daily tasks, and provide easier access to essential information.

In space, factors such as microgravity, radiation, isolation, sleep disturbances, and demanding work schedules can significantly affect astronauts' health and quality of life. To address these challenges, we aimed to develop an integrated digital platform that allows astronauts to monitor their health indicators and manage their daily activities efficiently.

Solar Pulse seeks to address these needs by combining health monitoring, mission planning, and artificial intelligence assistance into a single platform.

How Does Our Project Work?

Solar Pulse is built around three core systems.

1. Health Monitoring

Our system presents health indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), sleep patterns, physical activity, and other wellness metrics through intuitive dashboards and interactive charts.

In our current prototype, these measurements are simulated for demonstration purposes. In the future, we aim to improve health monitoring by integrating supported real sensor data from wearable devices such as the Samsung Galaxy Watch7.

2. Mission Planner

We developed a mission planning system that enables astronauts to organize their daily and weekly tasks.

Users can categorize their tasks, track completed activities, and manage their work schedules. The platform also includes achievement badges and personal development features designed to encourage healthy habits.

Our system is designed to support different mission scenarios, including the International Space Station (ISS), the Moon, Mars, and deep-space missions.

3. AI Assistant

We integrated the Qwen3.8-27B large language model into Solar Pulse.

User questions are transmitted through our FastAPI backend to the Qwen model running locally in LM Studio. The AI-generated responses are progressively displayed to users through streaming technology.

We successfully verified this integration in a local environment using real responses generated by the model.

Our next objective is to develop a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system that enables the AI assistant to provide information supported by reliable NASA scientific research, including source references.

Technologies and Tools We Used

We developed Solar Pulse using modern web technologies, a Python-based backend, and locally hosted artificial intelligence solutions.

  • React: Development of the user interface and interactive components.
  • TypeScript: Improving frontend code reliability and maintainability.
  • Vite: Frontend development and build infrastructure.
  • Python and FastAPI: Backend API development and processing AI requests.
  • Qwen3.8-27B: Large language model powering the AI assistant.
  • LM Studio: Running the AI model in a local environment.
  • REST API and Server-Sent Events (SSE): Communication between the frontend and backend, including streaming AI responses.
  • Fedora Linux: One of our development and local testing environments.

According to our development reports, we successfully passed a total of 55 automated tests, including 41 frontend tests and 14 backend tests.

We also conducted end-to-end communication tests using the actual Qwen model to verify that our AI integration works as intended.

What Makes Our Project Innovative?

Solar Pulse introduces an integrated approach by bringing astronaut health monitoring, mission management, and artificial intelligence assistance together within a single platform rather than relying on separate applications.

Our platform is designed not only to display health measurements but also to help astronauts manage their daily routines more efficiently and access reliable information about living and working in space.

Our ability to run the AI system locally also allows us to explore potential future applications in mission environments where internet connectivity may be limited or unreliable.

Additionally, we adopted a privacy-conscious approach that prioritizes user consent before personal information is shared with the AI assistant.

Factors Our Team Considered During Development

Throughout the development process, our team focused on several important factors, particularly user experience, data privacy, system reliability, accessibility, and the responsible presentation of health-related information.

We designed a clean, intuitive, and responsive interface that astronauts could navigate efficiently, even during demanding daily schedules.

We clearly distinguish simulated health measurements from real sensor data and do not position our AI assistant as a medical diagnostic system.

We also tested the existing features of our application and designed its architecture to support future integrations with real wearable sensors and more advanced scientific research systems.

Expected Impact and Future Goals

Through Solar Pulse, we aim to improve astronauts' health awareness, simplify mission organization, and support access to relevant information during long-duration space missions.

In future development stages, we plan to introduce real-time wearable sensor integration, AI-powered research assistance grounded in NASA scientific sources, secure data synchronization, and more advanced personalized features.

Our long-term vision is to transform Solar Pulse into a reliable, accessible, and integrated digital support platform that could assist astronauts in managing their health and daily activities during space missions.

Solar Pulse — Human First, Space Next.
